summary: Removed the "intro" and "details" steps before email collection, cutting the funnel from 6 to 4 steps, because each pre-commitment screen causes ~20% additional drop-off and users who land on a signup page are already interested enough to act — not to read company philosophy first.

Replaced the generic welcome page with a benefit-focused headline, three concise trust-building bullet points, a styled blue CTA button ("무료로 시작하기" / Start for free), and social proof showing 12,000 existing users — all of which reduce hesitation and create a clearer reason to click through immediately.

Replaced the passive welcome headline and "Learn more" link with a direct benefit headline ("Start right now"), a concrete time-to-signup promise ("30 seconds, all features free"), and a visually prominent styled CTA button — reducing cognitive friction and increasing click-through motivation.

Changed the CTA from "자세히 알아보기" (Learn more) to "무료로 시작하기" (Start for free) and replaced the friction-generating "read carefully before proceeding" message with a direct action prompt, because removing hesitation language and switching from a discovery CTA to a commitment CTA drives more users to click through to signup.

Replaced the passive "Welcome, read carefully before proceeding" + "Learn more" pattern with a concrete free-trial value prop and a direct action CTA ("Start free →"), removing the implied complexity that caused visitors to hesitate rather than click through to the email step.

Replaced the bare welcome page with a focused card that states the value proposition immediately, lists three concrete benefits, and replaces the passive "자세히 알아보기" link with a bold "무료로 시작하기" (Start for free) button — reducing visitor hesitation by making the offer and next action instantly clear.
